title: Adversarial product review: Relay
goal: Determine whether Relay solves a painful, distinct problem and identify what must be cut or proven before tomorrow's demo.
acceptanceCriteria: Give an unambiguous verdict: strong product, promising feature, or solution in search of a problem
Identify the single strongest user and incident wedge
Separate implemented behavior from demo simulation and roadmap
Name the three highest-leverage changes before the presentation

completed: Built a native orange Relay.app with visible SAIL provider status
Implemented scoped capability URLs, SHA-256 capsule integrity, expiry, secret scanning, receipts, and work-pod lifecycle
Ran a real Sailbox create, pause, resume, pull, and terminate loop
Implemented an autonomous backend harness boundary
Implemented a Greptile finding adapter that converts findings into typed operational memories
Built a one-button Greptile demo that seals six memories and warm-boots User 2
partial: Greptile input is currently a structured local demo fixture unless an authenticated adapter secret is configured
The public product name is Relay while internal protocol and package identifiers still use PassOn
The current full Node test runner hits a Node 24 native assertion associated with the Sail SDK environment
blocked: A real Greptile-reviewed demo PR has not yet been connected
No measured token, turn, or wall-clock savings exist yet

decisions: Position Greptile as repository intelligence and Relay as cross-operator continuity
Do not claim Greptile is an incident pager
Borrow Engramme's proactive memory thesis but use bounded, task-owned, expiring operational memory
Label all fixture-driven Greptile input as simulated
constraints: Tomorrow's judge demo must fit in three minutes
Never expose Sail keys, Greptile keys, capability tokens, or private repository content
The demo must show the actual Relay app, actual work-pod state, same digest, and User 2 receipt
No unsupported claims about benchmark scores or measured savings
rejectedApproaches: Calling a static mock a live integration
Positioning Relay as another general-purpose personal memory database
openQuestions: Is a cross-human and cross-agent incident handoff frequent and painful enough to support a company?
Is Relay a product, a protocol, or a feature Greptile and coding-agent vendors will absorb?
What is the smallest wedge that proves repeated use?
Does selected operational memory beat a strong generated summary under controlled evaluation?
Should the demo emphasize investigation handoff, PR ownership transfer, or autonomous long-horizon continuation?

validation.command: Browser: Relay Greptile finding → Resume as User 2
validation.result: Six memories sealed, SHA-256 digest shown, Codex acceptance receipt issued, no browser errors
Two pure adapter tests pass; server test is blocked by a Node 24 native runtime assertion

traceSummary: Be hostile to the thesis. Inspect the repository, distinguish working software from narrative, compare against Greptile Fix with Agent, Greptile MCP, Claude-Mem, Letta, and ordinary markdown handoffs, and recommend killing the project if the wedge is not real.
nextAction: Read the listed artifacts, run the demo locally if useful, then write a one-page investment and product critique with a go/no-go verdict.
stopConditions: Do not propose more infrastructure until the target user and repeated workflow are clear
Do not accept simulated integration evidence as proof of user demand
